newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African union says Implats strike on hold.
newsitem.headline: S.African union says Implats strike on hold.

text.p: South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Friday a strike planned for Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd had been put on hold pending a meeting of the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration next week.
NUM spokesman George Molebatsi told Reuters that union and management negotiators were now engaging the Commission, which had postponed a meeting scheduled for Friday to Monday.
"It has been postponed to Monday. The outcome of that will determine the (union) action," Molebatsi said.
"The feeling among the people down there is that they should go on strike," he said, but added that the union had put the strike on hold until further notice.
Implats said the NUM membership within the affected bargaining unit at Implats' Refineries totals 415 members.
The company said on Thursday it had received formal notification of strike action by the NUM.
On Friday Implats said all workers turned up for work.

Implats Refineries management and the NUM met on four occasions but settlement on annual wage increases could not be reached and the NUM declared a dispute which was referred to the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration.
Two further conciliation meetings were held after that but no settlement was achieved, Implats said.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, while the NUM's last offer was 19.2 percent.
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996.
